hints: Calculate key values of velocity at segment boundaries: at $t = 0, 5, 6, 7, 13.5$.
Note that $v = 2t + 1$ is a straight line from $(0, 1)$ to $(5, 11)$.
Note that $v = 36 - t^2$ is an inverted parabolic curve from $(5, 11)$, crossing the time axis at $(6, 0)$, to $(7, -13)$.
Note that $v = 2t - 27$ is a straight line from $(7, -13)$ returning to rest at $(13.5, 0)$.
walkthrough:
Evaluate the velocity at key transition points:
$$\text{For } 0 \le t \le 5: \quad v(0) = 1\text{ m s}^{-1}, \quad v(5) = 2(5) + 1 = 11\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
$$\text{For } 5 \le t \le 7: \quad v(5) = 36 - 25 = 11\text{ m s}^{-1}, \quad v(6) = 36 - 36 = 0, \quad v(7) = 36 - 49 = -13\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
$$\text{For } 7 \le t \le 13.5: \quad v(7) = 2(7) - 27 = -13\text{ m s}^{-1}, \quad v(13.5) = 2(13.5) - 27 = 0$$

Sketch the three connected segments:
1. A straight line segment with positive gradient $2$ joining $(0, 1)$ to $(5, 11)$.
2. A downward-opening quadratic curve from $(5, 11)$, crossing the $t$-axis at $(6, 0)$, down to $(7, -13)$.
3. A straight line segment with positive gradient $2$ from $(7, -13)$ up to $(13.5, 0)$.

ai_rubric.Interpreting Motion Graphs: Correctly sketches linear segment on $0 \le t \le 5$, parabolic curve on $5 \le t \le 7$ crossing at $t=6$, and linear segment on $7 \le t \le 13.5$ ending at $(13.5, 0)$.

teacher_walkthrough: Analyze the three stages of the piecewise velocity function to identify coordinates and curve types:
Phase 1 ($0 \le t \le 5$): The function $v = 2t + 1$ is linear with gradient $2$ and vertical intercept $1$. It connects the point $(0, 1)$ to the point $(5, 11)$.

Phase 2 ($5 \le t \le 7$): The function $v = 36 - t^2$ is an inverted parabola with vertex on the vertical axis at $(0, 36)$. It starts at $(5, 11)$, crosses the horizontal time axis at $t = \sqrt{36} = 6\text{ s}$, and reaches $(7, -13)$ at $t = 7\text{ s}$.

Phase 3 ($7 \le t \le 13.5$): The function $v = 2t - 27$ is linear with gradient $2$. It begins at $(7, -13)$ and rises steadily to meet the time axis at $t = \frac{27}{2} = 13.5\text{ s}$ where $v = 0$.

Draw the complete graph: ensure the parabolic section curves concave downwards between $t = 5$ and $t = 7$, and explicitly label the points $(0, 1)$, $(5, 11)$, $(6, 0)$, $(7, -13)$, and $(13.5, 0)$ on the axes.

hints: For $t = 6$, use the velocity definition for the interval $5 \le t \le 7$: $v = 36 - t^2$.
Differentiate $v$ with respect to $t$ to find acceleration: $a = \frac{dv}{dt}$.
walkthrough:
Identify the velocity expression applicable at $t = 6$, which lies in the interval $5 \le t \le 7$:
$$v(t) = 36 - t^2$$

Differentiate velocity with respect to time to find the acceleration function:
$$a(t) = \frac{dv}{dt} = \frac{d}{dt}(36 - t^2) = -2t$$

Evaluate the acceleration at $t = 6$:
$$a(6) = -2(6) = -12\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

ai_rubric.Differentiating Motion Functions: Differentiates $v = 36 - t^2$ to get $a = -2t$ and evaluates at $t=6$ to obtain $-12\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

teacher_walkthrough:
State the relationship between acceleration and velocity:
$$a = \frac{dv}{dt}$$

At $t = 6\text{ s}$, the time belongs to the second domain $5 \le t \le 7$, where $v(t) = 36 - t^2$. Differentiate with respect to $t$ using the power rule:
$$\frac{d}{dt}(36) = 0, \quad \frac{d}{dt}(-t^2) = -2t$$
$$a(t) = -2t$$

Substitute $t = 6$ into the acceleration expression:
$$a(6) = -2 \times 6 = -12\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

hints: Total distance is the total area between the velocity curve and the time axis: integrate $|v(t)|$ over $[0, 13.5]$.
Split the integral at $t = 6$, where velocity changes sign from positive to negative, as well as at segment boundaries $t = 5$ and $t = 7$.
Calculate the four separate areas: $\int_0^5 (2t+1)\,dt$, $\int_5^6 (36-t^2)\,dt$, $\left|\int_6^7 (36-t^2)\,dt\right|$, and $\left|\int_7^{13.5} (2t-27)\,dt\right|$.
Sum the four positive areas to find the total distance.
walkthrough:
Split the total distance into four regions where velocity is strictly positive or strictly negative:
$$s = \int_0^5 (2t+1)\,dt + \int_5^6 (36-t^2)\,dt + \left|\int_6^7 (36-t^2)\,dt\right| + \left|\int_7^{13.5} (2t-27)\,dt\right|$$

Evaluate Section 1 from $t = 0$ to $t = 5$:
$$d_1 = \left[t^2 + t\right]_0^5 = (25 + 5) - 0 = 30\text{ m}$$

Evaluate Section 2 from $t = 5$ to $t = 6$ (above axis):
$$d_2 = \left[36t - \frac{t^3}{3}\right]_5^6 = (216 - 72) - \left(180 - \frac{125}{3}\right) = 144 - \frac{415}{3} = \frac{17}{3}\text{ m}$$

Evaluate Section 3 from $t = 6$ to $t = 7$ (below axis):
$$d_3 = \left|\left[36t - \frac{t^3}{3}\right]_6^7\right| = \left|\left(252 - \frac{343}{3}\right) - 144\right| = \left|\frac{413}{3} - 144\right| = \left|-\frac{19}{3}\right| = \frac{19}{3}\text{ m}$$

Evaluate Section 4 from $t = 7$ to $t = 13.5$ (triangle below axis with base $6.5\text{ s}$ and height $13\text{ m s}^{-1}$):
$$d_4 = \frac{1}{2} \times (13.5 - 7) \times 13 = \frac{1}{2}(6.5)(13) = 42.25\text{ m}$$

Sum all four contributions to find the total distance:
$$s = 30 + \frac{17}{3} + \frac{19}{3} + 42.25 = 30 + 12 + 42.25 = 84.25\text{ m}$$

ai_rubric.Integrating Motion Functions: Sets up piecewise integrals splitting at $t=6$, integrates correctly with antiderivatives $t^2+t$, $36t - t^3/3$, and obtains total distance $84.25\text{ m}$.

teacher_walkthrough: To find the total distance rather than displacement, we must integrate the speed $|v(t)|$. From part (a), the velocity is positive on $0 \le t < 6$ and negative on $6 < t \le 13.5$. We divide the motion into four monotonic intervals:

Interval 3 ($6 \le t \le 7$, $v \le 0$):
Since $v \le 0$, the distance is the negative of the definite integral:
$$d_3 = -\int_6^7 (36 - t^2)\,dt = \int_6^7 (t^2 - 36)\,dt = \left[\frac{t^3}{3} - 36t\right]_6^7$$
At $t = 7$:
$$\frac{7^3}{3} - 36(7) = \frac{343}{3} - 252 = \frac{343 - 756}{3} = -\frac{413}{3}$$
At $t = 6$:
$$\frac{6^3}{3} - 36(6) = 72 - 216 = -144 = -\frac{432}{3}$$
Subtract:
$$d_3 = -\frac{413}{3} - \left(-\frac{432}{3}\right) = \frac{19}{3}\text{ m}$$

Interval 4 ($7 \le t \le 13.5$, $v \le 0$):
This region is a right-angled triangle under the time axis with horizontal base $13.5 - 7 = 6.5\text{ s}$ and vertical height $|-13| = 13\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$d_4 = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times 6.5 \times 13 = \frac{84.5}{2} = 42.25\text{ m}$$

Sum the four distance components:
$$d = d_1 + d_2 + d_3 + d_4 = 30 + \frac{17}{3} + \frac{19}{3} + 42.25$$
Notice that $\frac{17}{3} + \frac{19}{3} = \frac{36}{3} = 12\text{ m}$:
$$d = 30 + 12 + 42.25 = 84.25\text{ m}$$
